newsitem.title: USA: Cash crudes strengthen in U.S., June grades fading.
newsitem.headline: Cash crudes strengthen in U.S., June grades fading.

text.p: U.S. cash crude grade differentials continued stronger late Thursday for July barrels, while outright cash steadied in-line with late NYMEX selling, traders said.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked flat at $21.80-90 a barrel, with June WTI some 20-25 cents weaker.

July Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) gained a sturdy 10 cents to move to a 15 cents premium against the futures price. Traders said expectations foreign crude deliveries against the June NYMEX contract would be rolled over for July propped cash over futures.
NYMEX said earlier Thursday that 2.349 million barrels of foreign crude was delivered against June paper contracts, out of a total monthly delivery of 2.372 million barrels.
Traders said most of the foreign crude was Nigerian Bonny Light, and likely the same crude delivered a month earlier against May paper matches.
Before June EFPs expired on Wednesday, premiums reached a plateau of 31 cents, traders noted.

As long as Bonny Light holds a lofty premium for deliveries against NYMEX, traders said EFPs would benefit. Bonny Light held a 60 cents premium for June, but was to shrink 20 cents to 40 cents on July 1.

For grade barrels, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was barely talked in June, while July barrels attracted firmer deals. Traders said July LLS was done from discounts of 15 to nine cents under benchmark WTI.
A wet Brent deal for a June 2-4 loader at a strong July Brent minus two cents supported LLS values, traders said.
Other July numbers saw West Texas Sour/Midland sell at a $1.50 discount, and Postings Plus around last trades of $2.06.
Jul/Aug spreads were nearly even at a one cents edge for August WTI/Cushing.
Other trades on Thursday saw June Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire move at WTI/Cushing -70 cents.
Jun/Jul spreads, or rolls, sold as low as minus seven cents, but talked late at minus 20-30 cents.
